data.exact_reserve_text: The change in the provisions for claims outstanding during the year was as follows: The following table presents the comparison of actual claims incurred to previous estimates for the last 10 years.
data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 2468 recorded a net prior-year release of approximately GBP 46.0m (about 9.8% of opening gross claims outstanding) for the year ended 31 December 2021. This release is driven by favourable claims development across older underwriting years (notably 2016-2018) as shown in the gross claims development table. The Syndicate states it does not have material COVID-19 exposure and the movements reflect ordinary development and re-estimation of prior-year ultimates.
raw_causal_phrases: fluctuations in the severity of claims compared with expectations, late reporting of claims, inadequate reserving and inadequate reinsurance protection (including the credit worthiness of major reinsurers).
Syndicate 2468 is judged not to have material insurance exposure to COVID-19 related claims and has experienced limited claims notifications in this regard during 2020 and 2021.

The 31st December 2021 technical provisions make allowance for potential claims arising in relation to this pandemic based on the detailed knowledge of business written and the expert judgements of actuarial and claims subject matter experts.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development figure was calculated from the gross claims development table (cumulative gross claims, GBP '000) by comparing current estimates to the prior diagonal for underwriting years 2016-2018 and excluding the two most recent underwriting years in the table. No explicit gross prior-year movement narrative figure was given. The technical provisions reconciliation line 'Change in estimates of technical provisions' was not used as a primary source because it includes current-year movements. Premiums and triangle are presented in GBP '000 in the report; amounts above are converted to millions. Gross premiums written are negative due to run-off activity.
